name: Terminal Damage
author: nyannoying
description: Beta. A broken car is no longer taken away: limp on, pull over or bring it in. Realistic failures with warning signs, a damage HUD, engineer radio, FIA rules, garage repairs and presets. Experimental and off by default: suspension damage from hits.

options.label: Preset
options.description: Casual: no random failures, forgiving rules. Realistic: real failure rates, FIA rules. Hardcore: Realistic, no damage panel, less power when broken. Launcher: applies at the next game start. In game: reopen this menu to see the changes.

options.label: Keep control after terminal damage
options.description: The heart of this addon. After a crash or a failure the game no longer takes your car and retires it: limp on, pull over or drive to your box, as the damage allows. Off: the game's own behaviour.

options.label: Power with a broken turbo/ERS part
options.description: Throttle left when the MGU-K, MGU-H, battery, turbo or control electronics fail and you limp on. A failed engine (ICE) or gearbox leaves no drive at all. Off: no drive either.

options.label: Engine sound off after a failure
options.description: A failed engine (ICE) plays the engine stop sound at once; terminal crash damage after 3-6 s; a retiring car standing still after 6 s. Then the engine stays silent.

options.label: Mechanical failures in Grand Prix
options.description: Random mechanical failures where the game has none (Grand Prix, custom races). Realistic: the real rate of the season below, fewer in short races. 10-50 %: the chance one part fails in the race. Not in Career.

values.label: Realistic for the season (see Failure season)

options.label: Failure season
options.description: For Realistic failures: how often cars broke down in that season and which parts, from real results. Pick your car mod's season. Often with warning signs first: lift and coast to nurse the part.

options.label: Keep control after a scripted failure
options.description: In Career and My Team the game can pull your car over and retire it after a mechanical failure. With this on, the car stays yours, but pit by the end of the next lap or retire it (see the next setting).

options.label: After a scripted failure or heavy damage, if you neither pit nor retire
options.description: As with a black flag with an orange disc: after the game's mechanical failure or heavy aero or body damage, pit by the end of the next lap, or retire. If you do neither, this decides: disqualified (the FIA penalty) or retired.

options.label: FIA red flag rules for a terminally damaged car
options.description: FIA rules at a red flag: no power unit or gearbox work is allowed, so a failed one retires the car, and so does a car left on track without drive. Accident damage on a car that still drives may be repaired (corner: dice roll).

options.label: Damage status panel
options.description: Icon tiles at the top right of the race HUD: engine, ERS, gearbox, brakes, suspension (with the corner, e.g. FL) and power, yellow, orange or red by how bad. Auto: only what is wrong. Always: all six on track. Off: none.

options.label: Engineer radio for damage and failures
options.description: Your engineer calls out warning signs, failures, brake problems and broken corners with the game's own voice lines. Off: no radio calls; the on-screen messages stay.

options.label: Retire in the radio menu
options.description: Adds Retire to the radio menu: pick it, then drive into your pit box, or pull over safely and stand still 10 s. Needs 'Keep control after terminal damage'. Needs a game restart after turning it on.

options.label: Retirement radio voice
options.description: When you pick Retire in the radio menu, your engineer answers with the stop-the-car line. Off: Retire still works, without the voice. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Retire in the pause menu: pull over first
options.description: On track, Retire in the pause menu does not end your race at once: drive into your pit box, or pull over safely and stand still 10 s. Off: it ends your race at once, as in the game.

options.label: Retire hotkey
options.description: Ctrl+Shift + the key below retires your car, damaged or not: drive into your pit box, or pull over safely and stand still 10 s (real drivers stop on track only with a problem). Press again to cancel.

options.label: Retire hotkey (with Ctrl+Shift)
options.description: The F key you press together with Ctrl+Shift to retire. Pick one no other mod uses.

options.label: Suspension damage from hits (experimental)
options.description: Experimental, off by default. Hits on a wheel can bend that corner (the car pulls), break it, or crack it so it fails later. While on, the game's own suspension damage stays stock, also with Heavier Damage. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Suspension damage for AI cars (experimental)
options.description: Experimental. AI cars that hit barriers or other cars can get a bent corner too, or a collapsed one: then they retire. Their game suspension damage stays stock too. Needs 'Suspension damage from hits' and a game restart.

options.label: Player wheel behavior
options.description: What a wheel torn off your car does. Stock: the game's tethers, the wheel hangs on and can jolt the car. Reduced jolting: tethers stay, the wheel can clip through the car. Loose: no tethers. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Loose AI wheels (no tethers)
options.description: A wheel torn off an AI car flies off as loose debris instead of hanging on its tethers. Separate from your own car's setting. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Retire in the pit box
options.description: With keep control: when you bring your broken car into your pit box, it retires there, as with Retire in the pause menu.

options.label: Crew pushes the car into the garage
options.description: With "Retire in the pit box": your crew pushes the broken car into the garage, then it retires. Retires in the box after 15 s if no push comes.

options.label: Garage crew in the race
options.description: Loads your garage push crew directly in a race. Restart required.

options.label: Garage crew assets in the race
options.description: The race also loads the garage crew scenes, so your crew can push a broken car in. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Experimental: clear retirement pit box
options.description: Hides tyre-stop equipment during a race retirement approach. Preserves the shared box while your teammate is pitting. Garage push crew remains visible.

options.label: Debug: UDP telemetry port
options.description: Debug. Not needed: the addon reads your speed from the game itself. Only for the debug telemetry log; leave it off if SimHub or another app uses the game's UDP. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Debug: fault type for the game's own failure
options.description: Debug. Only with 'Game's own failure' in Mechanical failures in Grand Prix: which fault the game applies.

options.label: Debug: hotkey triggers a failure
options.description: Debug, off by default. Test keys, all with Ctrl+Shift. F10: the engine (ICE) fails. F7: Career scripted failure. F6: the next partial failure. F9: throttle cap cycle. F4: test run of all faults (once: you drive, twice: the AI).

options.label: Debug: hotkey (with Ctrl+Shift)
options.description: The F key you press together with Ctrl+Shift for the debug failure. Pick one no other mod uses.

options.label: Debug: failing part
options.description: The part the debug hotkey breaks: 0 engine (ICE), 1 MGU-K, 2 MGU-H, 3 battery, 4 turbo, 5 control electronics, 6 gearbox.

options.label: Debug: crash limp roll
options.description: Debug. After a crash that broke one corner: can the car crawl on? Random: collapsed suspension 85 % front, 60 % rear; front wheel coming loose 35 %; never once the game tears the wheel off (its engine stops). Success or Fail forces the result.

options.label: Debug: red flag repair roll
options.description: Debug. At a red flag: does your team rebuild the broken corner of a car that crawled in? Random: 80 % for a suspension, 50 % for a lost wheel. Success or Fail forces the result.

options.label: Debug: garage corner repair time
options.description: Debug. Practice and qualifying garage repairs. Normal: a broken corner 20-30 min (a lost wheel 30-45), a damaged one 4-20 min. Fast: about a minute.

options.label: Debug: suspension test
options.description: Test only. Ctrl+Shift+F8 steps a change on your front-left wheel: toe, camber or suspension damage. Needs a game restart after changing it.

options.label: Debug: performance counters
options.description: Logs the time this addon's hooks take every 10 s to loader.log (not the game's own work or the GPU). Turn it on only to look into FPS drops.

options.label: Debug: garage crew diagnostics
options.description: Logs garage crew and asset details to swofty/loader.log. Needs a game restart.

options.label: Debug: log telemetry
options.description: Writes speed, rpm, gear and position of your car to swofty/loader.log.
